question:
______ are known as the powerhouses of the cell.

[SSC GD 2022]
options: Lysosomes
Mitochondria
Nucleus
Ribosome
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Mitochondria

Explanation:
Mitochondria are called the 'powerhouses of the cell' because they generate energy in the form of ATP (Adenosine Triphosphate) through cellular respiration. This process involves the oxidation of glucose, releasing energy. Mitochondria contain structures called cristae, which increase the surface area for energy production. They also have their own DNA, making them semi-autonomous organelles.

Extra Facts:
☛ Mitochondria were discovered by Kolliker in 1880.
☛ They are found in both plant and animal cells but are more abundant in animal cells.
☛ Mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) is inherited maternally and is used in forensic science and ancestry studies.
☛ Defects in mitochondrial DNA can lead to disorders like Leber's Hereditary Optic Neuropathy (LHON).

question:
Who among the following was the first Biologist who discovered cells?

[SSC MTS 2022]
options: Robert Hooke
Rosalind Franklin
Gregor Mendel
Charles Darwin
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Robert Hooke

Explanation:
Robert Hooke is credited as the first biologist to discover cells. In 1665, he described cells in his book 'Micrographia'. Hooke observed a thin slice of cork under a microscope and noticed small, room-like structures, which he named 'cells'. This discovery was a significant milestone in biology and laid the foundation for the 'Cell Theory'.

Extra Facts:
According to the Cell Theory, all living organisms are composed of cells, and the cell is the basic unit of life. This theory was later developed by Matthias Schleiden and Theodor Schwann in 1839. Robert Hooke not only discovered cells but also formulated 'Hooke's Law', which is related to the principle of elasticity in physics.

question_hi:
निम्नलिखित में से कौन कोशिकाओं की खोज करने वाला पहला जीव विज्ञानी था?

[SSC MTS 2022]
options_hi: रॉबर्ट हुक (Robert Hooke)
रॉसलिंड फ्रेंक्लिन (Rosalind Franklin)
ग्रेगर मेंडल (Gregor Mendel)
चार्ल्स डार्विन (Charles Darwin)
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है रॉबर्ट हुक (Robert Hooke)

Explanation:
रॉबर्ट हुक (Robert Hooke) को कोशिकाओं की खोज करने वाला पहला जीव विज्ञानी माना जाता है। उन्होंने 1665 में 'माइक्रोग्राफिया' नामक पुस्तक में कोशिकाओं का वर्णन किया था। हुक ने कॉर्क की पतली परत को माइक्रोस्कोप से देखा और उसमें छोटे-छोटे कमरे जैसी संरचनाएँ देखीं, जिन्हें उन्होंने 'सेल्स' (कोशिकाएँ) नाम दिया। यह खोज जीव विज्ञान में एक महत्वपूर्ण मील का पत्थर साबित हुई और 'कोशिका सिद्धांत' (Cell Theory) की नींव रखी।

Extra Facts:
कोशिका सिद्धांत के अनुसार, सभी जीव कोशिकाओं से बने होते हैं और कोशिका ही जीवन की मूलभूत इकाई है। इस सिद्धांत को बाद में मैथियास श्लाइडेन (Matthias Schleiden) और थियोडोर श्वान (Theodor Schwann) ने 1839 में और विकसित किया। रॉबर्ट हुक ने न केवल कोशिकाओं की खोज की बल्कि उन्होंने 'हुक का नियम' (Hooke's Law) भी प्रतिपादित किया, जो भौतिकी में प्रत्यास्थता के सिद्धांत से संबंधित है।

question:
Which of the following statements is correct regarding cell membrane?
I. The membrane is selectively permeable to some molecules present on either side of it.
II. Water may also move across this membrane from lower to higher concentration.

[SSC CGL 2023]
options: Only II
Only I
Neither I nor II
Both I and II
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Only I

Explanation:
The cell membrane is a selectively permeable membrane that allows only certain molecules to pass through it based on their size, charge, and polarity. It consists of a lipid bilayer and proteins, regulating molecular movement. Thus, statement I is correct.

Statement II is incorrect because water typically moves from higher to lower concentration (osmosis). Movement from lower to higher concentration requires energy (ATP), known as active transport, which does not apply to water.

Extra Facts:
Cell membranes contain protein channels (e.g., aquaporins) that facilitate rapid water movement. Selective permeability maintains cellular homeostasis. Additionally, glycolipids and glycoproteins aid in cell recognition and signaling.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams
☛ What is the cell membrane made of? → Lipid bilayer and proteins
☛ What is osmosis? → Water movement from high to low concentration
☛ Define active transport. → Energy (ATP)-driven movement of molecules against the concentration gradient
☛ Why is mitochondria called the powerhouse? → It produces ATP
☛ Plant cell walls are composed of? → Cellulose
question_hi:
कोशिका झिल्ली के संबंध में निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा कथन सही है?
I. झिल्ली इसके दोनों ओर मौजूद कुछ अणुओं के लिए चुनिंदा रूप से पारगम्य होती है।
II. पानी भी इस झिल्ली से होकर निम्न से उच्च सांद्रता में जा सकता है।

[SSC CGL 2023]
options_hi: केवल II
केवल I
न तो I और न ही II
I और II दोनों
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है केवल I

Explanation:
कोशिका झिल्ली एक चयनात्मक पारगम्य (selectively permeable) झिल्ली है, जो कुछ अणुओं को ही अपने अंदर या बाहर जाने देती है। यह झिल्ली लिपिड बाईलेयर और प्रोटीन से बनी होती है, जो अणुओं के आकार, आवेश और ध्रुवीयता के आधार पर उनके प्रवाह को नियंत्रित करती है। इस प्रकार, कथन I सही है।

कथन II गलत है क्योंकि पानी सामान्यतः उच्च सांद्रता से निम्न सांद्रता की ओर ही प्रवाहित होता है (अपोहन/ऑस्मोसिस)। निम्न से उच्च सांद्रता में जाने के लिए ऊर्जा (ATP) की आवश्यकता होती है, जिसे सक्रिय परिवहन कहते हैं, लेकिन यह प्रक्रिया पानी के लिए नहीं होती।

Extra Facts:
कोशिका झिल्ली में प्रोटीन चैनल्स (जैसे एक्वापोरिन) पानी के तेजी से प्रवाह में मदद करते हैं। झिल्ली की चयनात्मक पारगम्यता कोशिका के होमियोस्टेसिस (साम्यावस्था) को बनाए रखने में महत्वपूर्ण भूमिका निभाती है। इसके अलावा, ग्लाइकोलिपिड्स और ग्लाइकोप्रोटीन्स कोशिका को पहचान और संकेतन में मदद करते हैं।

☛ सक्रिय परिवहन क्या है? → ऊर्जा (ATP) का उपयोग करके अणुओं का निम्न से उच्च सांद्रता में परिवहन

question:
Plant cells differ from animal cells in having an additional layer around the cell membrane termed as ____________.

[SSC CHSL 2022]
options: Cytoplasm
Vacuole
Cell wall
Chloroplast
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Cell wall

Explanation:
Plant cells differ from animal cells because they have an additional layer around the cell membrane called the 'cell wall'. This layer is primarily made of cellulose and provides structural support to the cell. It offers mechanical protection and helps maintain the cell's shape. Animal cells lack this layer. Additionally, plant cells contain large vacuoles and chloroplasts, which are absent in animal cells.

Extra Facts:
The cell wall is not only found in plant cells but also in fungi, bacteria, and some protists, although their composition differs. For example, bacterial cell walls are made of peptidoglycan. The cell wall helps plants withstand turgor pressure and plays a crucial role in water absorption.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams

☛ What is the cell wall primarily made of? → Cellulose
☛ Which structure is absent in animal cells? → Cell wall
☛ What are the green pigments in plant cells called? → Chloroplasts
☛ What is the large vacuole in plant cells called? → Central vacuole
question_hi:
पादप कोशिकाएं जंतु कोशिकाओं से भिन्न होती हैं क्योंकि उनमें कोशिका झिल्ली के चारों ओर एक अतिरिक्त परत होती है जिसे __________. कहा जाता है।

solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है कोशिका भित्ति (Cell wall)

Explanation:
पादप कोशिकाएं जंतु कोशिकाओं से भिन्न होती हैं क्योंकि उनमें कोशिका झिल्ली के चारों ओर एक अतिरिक्त परत होती है जिसे 'कोशिका भित्ति' कहा जाता है। यह परत मुख्य रूप से सेल्यूलोज से बनी होती है और कोशिका को संरचनात्मक सहायता प्रदान करती है। यह कोशिका को यांत्रिक सुरक्षा देती है और कोशिका के आकार को बनाए रखने में मदद करती है। जंतु कोशिकाओं में यह परत अनुपस्थित होती है। इसके अलावा, पादप कोशिकाओं में बड़ी रिक्तिकाएं (Vacuoles) और हरितलवक (Chloroplasts) भी पाए जाते हैं, जो जंतु कोशिकाओं में नहीं होते हैं।

Extra Facts:
कोशिका भित्ति न केवल पादप कोशिकाओं में पाई जाती है, बल्कि कवक (Fungi), बैक्टीरिया और कुछ प्रोटिस्ट में भी पाई जाती है, हालांकि उनकी संरचना अलग होती है। उदाहरण के लिए, बैक्टीरिया की कोशिका भित्ति पेप्टिडोग्लाइकन से बनी होती है। कोशिका भित्ति पादपों को तनाव और दबाव को सहन करने में मदद करती है और जल के अवशोषण में भी महत्वपूर्ण भूमिका निभाती है।

question:
Mitochondria is not found in ______.

[SSC CGL 2023]
options: yeast
bacteria
algae
fungi
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is bacteria

Explanation:
Mitochondria is called the 'powerhouse of the cell' because it generates energy in the form of ATP (Adenosine Triphosphate). It is found in eukaryotic cells (e.g., yeast, algae, fungi) but is absent in prokaryotic cells (e.g., bacteria). Bacteria have a cell membrane, cell wall, ribosomes, and nucleoid, but they lack membrane-bound organelles like mitochondria, Golgi apparatus, and endoplasmic reticulum.

Extra Facts:
Mitochondria has its own DNA, called mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA), which is inherited maternally. The number of mitochondria depends on the energy requirements of the cell; for example, muscle cells have more mitochondria. Mitochondria was discovered in 1857 by Albert von Kölliker.

☛ Who discovered mitochondria? → Albert von Kölliker

question:
The smallest unit of the life capable of independent existence is:

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: Protoplasm
Vacuoles
Cytoplasm
Cell
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Cell

Explanation:
The cell is the smallest unit of life capable of independent existence. It is the fundamental structural and functional unit of all living organisms. A cell carries out all essential life processes such as metabolism, growth, reproduction, and response to stimuli. Robert Hooke discovered the cell in 1665. According to the cell theory, all living organisms are composed of cells, and new cells arise from pre-existing cells. Protoplasm, vacuoles, and cytoplasm are components of a cell, but they cannot exist independently.

Extra Facts:
Cells are of two types: prokaryotic (e.g., bacteria) and eukaryotic (e.g., plants and animals). Eukaryotic cells are more complex and contain a true nucleus. The cell membrane (plasma membrane) separates the cell from its external environment and regulates the exchange of materials. Mitochondria are called the powerhouse of the cell because they generate ATP (energy). Plastids (chloroplasts) are found only in plant cells and are responsible for photosynthesis.

Extra Facts:
कोशिकाएं दो प्रकार की होती हैं: प्रोकैरियोटिक (जैसे बैक्टीरिया) और यूकैरियोटिक (जैसे पौधे और जंतु)। यूकैरियोटिक कोशिकाएं अधिक जटिल होती हैं और इनमें एक सच्चा केन्द्रक होता है। कोशिका झिल्ली (प्लाज्मा मेम्ब्रेन) कोशिका को बाहरी वातावरण से अलग करती है और पदार्थों के आदान-प्रदान को नियंत्रित करती है। माइटोकॉन्ड्रिया को कोशिका का पावरहाउस कहा जाता है क्योंकि यह एटीपी (ऊर्जा) उत्पन्न करता है। प्लास्टिड (क्लोरोप्लास्ट) केवल पादप कोशिकाओं में पाए जाते हैं और प्रकाश संश्लेषण के लिए जिम्मेदार होते हैं।

question:
Which cytologist demonstrated the role of the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) in protein processing and sorting in a variety of cells in the 1960s ?

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: Ralph M Steinman
George E Palade
Nettie Stevens
Cyril Darlington
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is George E Palade

Explanation:
George E Palade was a renowned cytologist who in the 1960s elucidated the role of the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) in protein processing and sorting in various cells. Using electron microscopy techniques, he studied the structure and function of cells. Palade demonstrated that the ER plays a crucial role in protein synthesis, transport, and modification within the cell. For this contribution, he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Medicine in 1974. The ER exists in two forms: rough ER (associated with ribosomes) and smooth ER (involved in lipid synthesis).

Extra Facts:
The endoplasmic reticulum (ER) is a vital organelle involved in the synthesis, transport, and detoxification of proteins and lipids. The rough ER is studded with ribosomes and participates in protein synthesis, while the smooth ER aids in lipid synthesis and calcium ion storage. Apart from Palade, Camillo Golgi discovered the Golgi apparatus, which modifies and packages proteins. The ER and Golgi apparatus work together in the secretory pathway of eukaryotic cells.

question:
Where will you find plastids in a leaf cell?

[SSC GD 2022]
options: nucleus
cell wall
cytoplasm
cell membrane
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is cytoplasm

Explanation:
In leaf cells, plastids are found in the cytoplasm. Plastids are essential organelles in plant cells that aid in photosynthesis and food storage. The most prominent among them are chloroplasts, which contain chlorophyll and are crucial for the process of photosynthesis. Plastids float freely in the cytoplasm and assist in various cellular functions. They are not found in the nucleus, cell wall, or cell membrane.

Extra Facts:
There are three types of plastids:
1. Chloroplast: Green in color and responsible for photosynthesis.
2. Chromoplast: Yellow, orange, or red in color, providing color to fruits and flowers.
3. Leucoplast: Colorless and involved in food storage, such as starch.
Plastids are found only in plant cells, not in animal cells.

question:
Which of the following organelle of the eukaryotic cells are also called suicidal bags?

[NTPC CBT 2]
options: Golgi body
Mitochondria
Lysosomes
Chloroplast
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Lysosomes

Explanation:
Lysosomes are called 'suicidal bags' because they contain digestive enzymes (hydrolytic enzymes) that break down damaged or unnecessary parts of the cell. When the cell is damaged or dies, lysosomes burst and release their enzymes into the cell, leading to the digestion of the cell. This process is called 'autolysis'. This process causes the self-destruction of the cell, hence lysosomes are called 'suicidal bags'. Lysosomes are important organelles found in eukaryotic cells that play a crucial role in cellular cleaning and recycling.

Extra Facts:
Lysosomes were discovered in 1955 by Christian de Duve. They are primarily found in animal cells but are also present in some plant cells. Lysosomes contain over 40 types of hydrolytic enzymes capable of breaking down proteins, lipids, carbohydrates, and nucleic acids. Deficiency or malfunction of lysosomes can lead to several genetic disorders such as Tay-Sachs disease and Gaucher's disease.

Solution: Correct Answer is Golgi apparatus

Explanation:
The Golgi apparatus is the organelle responsible for transporting, modifying, and packaging proteins and lipids into vesicles. It receives molecules from the endoplasmic reticulum (ER), modifies them (e.g., through glycosylation), and packages them into vesicles for transport to various parts of the cell or outside the cell membrane. The Golgi apparatus plays a crucial role in the secretory pathway and is also involved in the formation of lysosomes. It acts as the 'traffic police' of the cell, ensuring proper distribution of cellular products.

Extra Facts:
The Golgi apparatus was discovered by Camillo Golgi in 1898. It consists of a series of flattened membrane-bound sacs called cisternae. In plant cells, it contributes to the formation of the cell wall. The Golgi apparatus is part of the endomembrane system and works closely with the ER. It is particularly prominent in cells that secrete large amounts of proteins, such as pancreatic cells.

question:
In the process of cell division, the formation of phragmoplast between the two daughter nuclei occurs during:

[SSC MTS 2023]
options: the G0 phase
the cytokinesis
the S phase
the Karyokinesis
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is the cytokinesis

Explanation:
The phragmoplast is a structure formed during cytokinesis in plant cells. It helps in the formation of a cell plate between the two daughter nuclei, which eventually develops into a new cell wall. Cytokinesis is the stage of the cell cycle where the cytoplasm divides to form two separate cells. This process occurs after karyokinesis, where the nucleus divides.

Extra Facts:
- In plant cells, cytokinesis occurs via the phragmoplast, whereas in animal cells, a cleavage furrow forms.
- The stages of the cell cycle are: G1, S, G2 (interphase), M (mitosis). DNA replication occurs in the S phase, while nuclear division (karyokinesis) and cytoplasmic division (cytokinesis) occur in the M phase.
- The G0 phase is a resting state where cells do not divide.

solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है कोशिकाद्रव्य विभाजन

Explanation:
फ्रैग्मोप्लास्ट (phragmoplast) एक संरचना है जो पादप कोशिकाओं में कोशिकाद्रव्य विभाजन (cytokinesis) के दौरान बनती है। यह दो संतति केन्द्रकों के बीच एक साइटोकाइनेटिक प्लेट (cell plate) के निर्माण में मदद करता है, जो अंततः नई कोशिका भित्ति (cell wall) बनाती है। कोशिकाद्रव्य विभाजन, कोशिका चक्र का वह चरण है जिसमें कोशिका का साइटोप्लाज्म विभाजित होकर दो अलग-अलग कोशिकाएँ बनाता है। यह प्रक्रिया केंद्रकभाजन (karyokinesis) के बाद होती है, जिसमें केन्द्रक का विभाजन होता है।

- कोशिका चक्र के चरण हैं: G1, S, G2 (इंटरफेज), M (माइटोसिस)। S चरण में DNA प्रतिकृति (replication) होती है, जबकि M चरण में केंद्रकभाजन और कोशिकाद्रव्य विभाजन होता है।
- G0 चरण एक विश्राम अवस्था है जहाँ कोशिका विभाजन नहीं करती।

question:
Which of the following is present only in plant cells?

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: Nucleus
Golgi apparatus
Plastids
Mitochondria
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Plastids

Explanation:
Plastids are organelles found exclusively in plant cells. They are double-membrane-bound structures involved in photosynthesis (chloroplasts), pigment storage (chromoplasts), and food storage (leucoplasts). Animal cells lack plastids. Other options like the nucleus (present in all eukaryotic cells), Golgi apparatus (for protein modification and packaging), and mitochondria (energy production) are present in both plant and animal cells.

Extra Facts:
Chloroplasts contain chlorophyll, essential for photosynthesis. Plastids have their own DNA and can replicate independently. They were discovered by Ernst Haeckel. Plastids give plant cells unique colors (e.g., green leaves) and nutrient storage capabilities.

question:
Which of the following is NOT one of the three main parts of the cell?

[SSC MTS 2022]
options: Nucleus
Cytoplasm
Vacuole
Cell membrane
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Vacuole

Explanation:
The three main parts of a cell are: Nucleus, Cytoplasm, and Cell membrane. The nucleus is the control center of the cell containing genetic material (DNA). Cytoplasm is a jelly-like substance that contains all the organelles. The cell membrane is a semi-permeable membrane that defines the boundary of the cell and regulates the movement of substances in and out of the cell. Vacuole is an organelle mainly found in plant cells that stores water, minerals, and waste materials. It is not one of the three main parts of the cell.

Extra Facts:
The cell is the fundamental unit of life. In plant cells, vacuoles are large and provide structural support. Animal cells may have small or absent vacuoles. The cell membrane is made of lipids and proteins and separates the cell from the external environment. The cytoplasm contains organelles like mitochondria, ribosomes, and Golgi apparatus, which are responsible for various biological functions.

question:
Which cellular structure controls cell motility, adhesion, and polarity at interphase, and facilitates the organisation of spindle poles during mitosis ?

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: Centrosomes
Peroxisomes
Lysosomes
Glyoxysomes
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Centrosomes

Explanation:
The centrosome is a crucial cellular organelle that primarily controls cell motility, adhesion, and polarity during interphase. It also plays a vital role in organizing the spindle poles during mitosis. The centrosome contains two centrioles that serve as the microtubule-organizing center (MTOC). These microtubules are essential for cell shape, movement, and division. The absence or dysfunction of centrosomes can lead to errors in cell division, potentially causing diseases like cancer.

Extra Facts:
The centrosome is found in animal cells but is absent in most higher plant cells. It plays a key role in various stages of the cell cycle. Research on centrosomes is significant for understanding cell division and diseases like cancer. Additionally, the centrosome participates in forming the primary cilium, which is important for cell signaling.

सेंट्रोसोम कोशिका का एक महत्वपूर्ण अंग है जो मुख्य रूप से अंतरावस्था (interphase) में कोशिका की गतिशीलता, आसंजन और ध्रुवता को नियंत्रित करता है। यह समसूत्रण (mitosis) के दौरान स्पिंडल ध्रुवों के संगठन में भी महत्वपूर्ण भूमिका निभाता है। सेंट्रोसोम में दो सेंट्रिओल होते हैं जो माइक्रोट्यूब्यूल्स के संगठन केंद्र के रूप में कार्य करते हैं। ये माइक्रोट्यूब्यूल्स कोशिका के आकार, गति और विभाजन के लिए आवश्यक होते हैं। सेंट्रोसोम की अनुपस्थिति या दोष कोशिका विभाजन में गड़बड़ी पैदा कर सकता है, जिससे कैंसर जैसी बीमारियाँ हो सकती हैं।

Extra Facts:
सेंट्रोसोम पशु कोशिकाओं में पाया जाता है, लेकिन अधिकांश उच्च पादप कोशिकाओं में अनुपस्थित होता है। यह कोशिका चक्र के विभिन्न चरणों में महत्वपूर्ण भूमिका निभाता है। सेंट्रोसोम का अध्ययन कोशिका विभाजन और कैंसर जैसी बीमारियों के शोध में महत्वपूर्ण है। इसके अलावा, सेंट्रोसोम प्राथमिक सिलिया (primary cilium) के निर्माण में भी भाग लेता है, जो कोशिका संकेतन (cell signaling) में महत्वपूर्ण है।

question:
Select the correct statement.

[SSC CGL 2023]
options: Mitochondria and nucleus are found in bacteria.
Ribosomes, mitochondria and lysosomes are found in animal cells.
Chloroplast, ribosomes and nucleus are present in fungal cells.
Mitochondria and nucleus are absent in plant cells.
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Ribosomes, mitochondria and lysosomes are found in animal cells.

Explanation:
Animal cells contain organelles such as ribosomes, mitochondria, and lysosomes. Ribosomes are responsible for protein synthesis. Mitochondria, known as the 'powerhouse of the cell', produce ATP (adenosine triphosphate), which provides energy for cellular activities. Lysosomes, often called the 'suicidal bags' of the cell, contain digestive enzymes that break down waste materials and cellular debris. These organelles are essential for the proper functioning of animal cells. The other options are incorrect because bacteria lack mitochondria and a true nucleus, fungal cells do not contain chloroplasts, and plant cells possess both mitochondria and a nucleus.

Extra Facts:
Animal cells lack a cell wall and chloroplasts, which are present in plant cells. Bacteria are prokaryotic cells, meaning they do not have a nucleus or membrane-bound organelles. Fungal cells are eukaryotic but do not contain chloroplasts as they do not perform photosynthesis. Lysosomes are found only in eukaryotic cells and are formed by the Golgi apparatus. The presence of these organelles distinguishes eukaryotic cells (animal, plant, fungi) from prokaryotic cells (bacteria).

question:
______is the fluid content inside the plasma membrane.

[SSC GD 2022]
options: mitochondria
nucleus
cytoplasm
chromatin
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is cytoplasm

Explanation:
Cytoplasm is the jelly-like substance found inside the plasma membrane that surrounds all the organelles within the cell. It is a colloidal solution containing water, proteins, lipids, carbohydrates, mineral salts, and other organic compounds. The cytoplasm is essential for various metabolic activities of the cell and aids in the transport of materials between organelles. It also provides structural support to the cell.

Extra Facts:
The cytoplasm consists of two parts: the cytosol (a liquid medium) and the organelles (such as mitochondria, ribosomes, etc.). In plant cells, cytoplasmic streaming (cyclosis) can be observed, which helps in the transport of materials. The cytoplasm also contains enzymes that catalyze various metabolic reactions.

question:
Which structure within the nucleus contains genetic information in the form of DNA?

[SSC MTS 2024]
options: Ribosome
Chromosome
Nucleolus
Vacuole
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Chromosome

Explanation:
The chromosome is the structure within the nucleus that contains genetic information in the form of DNA (Deoxyribonucleic Acid). DNA is a long molecular chain organized into functional units called genes, which control protein synthesis and various biological processes. Chromosomes are made up of DNA tightly coiled around proteins called histones, forming a condensed structure that facilitates DNA organization and division during cell replication. Humans have 23 pairs (46) of chromosomes, inherited equally from both parents.

Extra Facts:
- Chromosomes were first discovered by Walther Flemming in 1882.
- Each chromosome consists of two chromatids joined at the centromere.
- The double-helix model of DNA was proposed by James Watson and Francis Crick in 1953.
- Mitochondria also contain a small amount of DNA, known as mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA).

question:
In which year did Walther Flemming coined the term ‘chromatin’ for the stained substance found in the cell nucleus?

[SSC CGL 2023]
options: 1900
1840
1849
1879
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 1879

Explanation:
Walther Flemming coined the term ‘chromatin’ in 1879 for the stained substance found in the cell nucleus. While studying cell division (mitosis), Flemming discovered this material. Chromatin is a complex of DNA and proteins that condenses into chromosomes during cell division. It plays a crucial role in transferring genetic information from one generation to the next. Flemming's contribution laid the foundation for significant advancements in cell biology and genetics.

Extra Facts:
Chromatin exists in two forms: euchromatin (active, less condensed) and heterochromatin (inactive, highly condensed). It dynamically changes during the cell cycle. The study of chromatin structure is vital in molecular biology and genetic engineering. Flemming used various dyes to visualize cellular structures, aiding in understanding the process of cell division.

question:
Which of the given options is rod-shaped, carries genetic information, is visible only at cell division and is present in the nucleus?

[SSC MTS 2024]
options: Chromosomes
Lysosomes
Ribosomes
Cytoplasm
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Chromosomes

Explanation:
Chromosomes are rod-shaped structures that carry genetic information (DNA). They become visible only during cell division when chromatin condenses to form chromosomes. Chromosomes are present in the nucleus of the cell, and their number is fixed for each species. For example, humans have 23 pairs (46) of chromosomes. Chromosomes play a crucial role in heredity and the transmission of genetic traits.

Extra Facts:
Chromosomes are made up of DNA and proteins (histones). Outside of cell division, chromosomes exist as chromatin, which is a less condensed form. Chromosomes are responsible for sex determination and the inheritance of genetic traits. Genetic disorders like Down syndrome occur due to chromosomal abnormalities. The study of chromosomes is called cytogenetics.

question:
The transportation mechanism in cells by which food or other useful molecules from the outside are carried inside the cell is known as ___________.

[SSC MTS 2024]
options: Osmosis
Fusion
Endocytosis
Exocytosis
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Endocytosis

Explanation:
Endocytosis is the process by which the cell membrane engulfs food or other useful molecules from the outside and transports them inside the cell. This occurs when a part of the cell membrane folds inward, forming a 'vesicle' that carries the molecules into the cell. There are three types of endocytosis: Phagocytosis (engulfing solid particles), Pinocytosis (engulfing liquid droplets), and Receptor-mediated endocytosis (specific molecule uptake). This mechanism is crucial for the cell to absorb essential nutrients and maintain cellular functions.

Extra Facts:
Endocytosis and exocytosis are both examples of active transport, requiring energy (ATP). Endocytosis plays a vital role in the immune system, where white blood cells destroy pathogens through phagocytosis. In contrast, exocytosis is the process by which cells expel waste materials or secrete substances (e.g., hormones) outside the cell. The Golgi apparatus is often involved in modifying and packaging materials for exocytosis.

solution_hi:

Explanation:
अंतःकोशिकता (Endocytosis) वह प्रक्रिया है जिसमें कोशिका झिल्ली (cell membrane) बाहर से भोजन या अन्य उपयोगी अणुओं को कोशिका के अंदर ले जाती है। यह प्रक्रिया कोशिका झिल्ली के एक हिस्से के अंदर की ओर मुड़ने से होती है, जिससे एक 'वेसिकल' (vesicle) बनता है जो अणुओं को कोशिका के अंदर ले जाता है। अंतःकोशिकता तीन प्रकार की होती है: फागोसाइटोसिस (ठोस कणों का अंतर्ग्रहण), पिनोसाइटोसिस (तरल पदार्थों का अंतर्ग्रहण), और रिसेप्टर-मध्यस्थ अंतःकोशिकता (विशिष्ट अणुओं का अंतर्ग्रहण)। यह प्रक्रिया कोशिका के लिए आवश्यक पोषक तत्वों को ग्रहण करने में महत्वपूर्ण भूमिका निभाती है।

Extra Facts:
अंतःकोशिकता (Endocytosis) और बहिःकोशिकता (Exocytosis) दोनों ही सक्रिय परिवहन (active transport) के उदाहरण हैं, जिसमें ऊर्जा (ATP) की आवश्यकता होती है। अंतःकोशिकता प्रतिरक्षा प्रणाली (immune system) में भी महत्वपूर्ण है, जहां श्वेत रक्त कोशिकाएं (white blood cells) रोगाणुओं को फागोसाइटोसिस द्वारा नष्ट करती हैं। इसके विपरीत, बहिःकोशिकता (Exocytosis) वह प्रक्रिया है जिसमें कोशिका अपशिष्ट पदार्थों या स्रावित पदार्थों (जैसे हार्मोन) को कोशिका से बाहर निकालती है।

question:
____________ are a kind of waste disposal system of the cell.

[SSC GD 2022]
options: Lysosome
Mitochondria
Ribosome
Vacuole
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Lysosome

Explanation:
Lysosomes act as the waste disposal system of the cell. These are small, spherical organelles containing digestive enzymes (hydrolytic enzymes) that break down proteins, carbohydrates, lipids, and other macromolecules for recycling. Lysosomes also destroy dead or damaged organelles, bacteria, and viruses inside the cell, keeping it clean and functional. They are called 'Suicidal Bags' because if a lysosome bursts, its enzymes can digest the entire cell. Lysosomes are essential for autophagy, a process where the cell recycles its own damaged components.

Extra Facts:
Lysosomes were discovered by Christian de Duve in 1955. They are primarily found in animal cells, while in plant cells, vacuoles perform similar functions. The enzymes in lysosomes, called acid hydrolases, work best at an acidic pH (4.5-5.0). Lysosomes play a key role in immune defense by digesting pathogens and in cellular repair through autophagy.

☛ What replaces lysosomes in plant cells? → Vacuole
☛ What type of enzymes are found in lysosomes? → Hydrolytic enzymes
☛ Why are lysosomes called suicidal bags? → They can destroy the cell

question:
Which of the following cells line the spongocoels and canals in members of the phylum Porifera?

[SSC CGL 2022]
options: Somatic cells
Collar cells
White cells
Sex cells
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Collar cells

Explanation:
In members of the phylum Porifera (sponges), the spongocoel and canals are lined by collar cells (choanocytes). These cells are characterized by their unique collar-like structure and a flagellum. Their primary function is to generate water flow and trap food particles (like bacteria and other microbes). Choanocytes are found on the inner surface of sponges and are also called "flame cells".

Extra Facts:
• Sponges lack true tissues or organs.
• They have porocytes, which form pores for water entry.
• The body structure of sponges includes a gelatinous substance called mesohyl, containing amoebocytes.
• Sponges can reproduce both asexually (by budding) and sexually (via gametes).

question:
The scentific study of a cell is called:

[SSC CGL 2019]
options: cytology
histology
physiology
taxonomy
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is cytology

Explanation:
Cytology is the scientific study of cells. It is the branch of science that studies the structure, function, chemical composition, and life cycle of cells. The cell is the fundamental unit of life, and all living organisms are composed of cells. Histology is the study of tissues, Physiology is the study of the functions of organisms, and Taxonomy is the classification of organisms.

Extra Facts:
Cytology has significant contributions in the medical field, especially in cancer diagnosis (cytological tests). Robert Hooke first discovered cells in 1665. Advanced techniques like electron microscopy and fluorescence microscopy are used in cytology. The study of cells has provided us with information about DNA, RNA, and protein synthesis.

हल: सही उत्तर है कोशिका विज्ञान (Cytology)

Explanation:
कोशिका विज्ञान (Cytology) कोशिकाओं का वैज्ञानिक अध्ययन है। यह विज्ञान की वह शाखा है जो कोशिकाओं की संरचना, कार्य, रासायनिक संगठन और उनके जीवन चक्र का अध्ययन करती है। कोशिका जीवन की मूलभूत इकाई है और सभी जीवित प्राणी कोशिकाओं से बने होते हैं। हिस्टोलॉजी (Histology) ऊतकों का अध्ययन है, शरीर विज्ञान (Physiology) जीवों के कार्यों का अध्ययन है, और टैक्सोनॉमी (Taxonomy) जीवों का वर्गीकरण है।

Extra Facts:
कोशिका विज्ञान का महत्वपूर्ण योगदान चिकित्सा क्षेत्र में है, विशेष रूप से कैंसर की पहचान (साइटोलॉजिकल टेस्ट) में। रॉबर्ट हुक ने सबसे पहले 1665 में कोशिका की खोज की थी। कोशिका विज्ञान में इलेक्ट्रॉन माइक्रोस्कोपी और फ्लोरोसेंट माइक्रोस्कोपी जैसी उन्नत तकनीकों का उपयोग किया जाता है। कोशिका के अध्ययन से ही हमें डीएनए, आरएनए और प्रोटीन संश्लेषण के बारे में जानकारी मिली है।

question:
Which component of the cell organelles principally performs the function of packaging materials, to be delivered either to the intra-cellular targets or secreted outside the cell?

[SSC MTS 2022]
options: Chloroplast
Mitochondria
Golgi Apparatus
Chromosomes
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Golgi Apparatus

Explanation:
The Golgi Apparatus is a cellular organelle primarily responsible for packaging materials such as proteins and lipids. It plays a crucial role in delivering these materials to intra-cellular targets or secreting them outside the cell. The Golgi modifies, sorts, and packages substances received from the Endoplasmic Reticulum (ER). It also aids in the formation of lysosomes. Structurally, the Golgi consists of a series of membrane-bound sacs called cisternae.

Extra Facts:
The Golgi Apparatus was discovered in 1898 by Camillo Golgi, after whom it is named. It is found in eukaryotic cells. Another important function of the Golgi is its involvement in the formation and repair of the cell membrane. It also participates in the synthesis of glycoproteins and glycolipids, which are essential for cell recognition and signaling.

कोशिकीय अंगक के किस घटक का मुख्य कार्य द्रव्य को संवेष्टित कर अंतर-कोशिकी लक्ष्य तक पहुँचाना या कोशिका के बाहर स्रवण करना है?

[SSC MTS 2022]
options_hi: हरितलवक
सूत्रकणिका ( माइटोकॉन्ड्रिया)
गॉल्जीकाय
गुणसूत्र
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है गॉल्जीकाय

Explanation:
गॉल्जीकाय (Golgi Apparatus) एक कोशिकीय अंगक है जिसका मुख्य कार्य प्रोटीन और लिपिड जैसे पदार्थों को संवेष्टित (package) करना है। यह अंतर-कोशिकीय लक्ष्यों तक इन पदार्थों को पहुँचाने या कोशिका के बाहर स्रवित (secrete) करने में महत्वपूर्ण भूमिका निभाता है। गॉल्जीकाय एंडोप्लाज्मिक रेटिकुलम (ER) से प्राप्त पदार्थों को संशोधित (modify), छाँट (sort) और पैक करता है। यह लाइसोसोम के निर्माण में भी सहायता करता है। गॉल्जीकाय की संरचना सिस्टर्नी (cisternae) नामक झिल्लीदार थैलियों की श्रृंखला से बनी होती है।

Extra Facts:
गॉल्जीकाय की खोज 1898 में कैमिलो गॉल्जी (Camillo Golgi) ने की थी, जिसके नाम पर इसका नाम रखा गया। यह यूकेरियोटिक कोशिकाओं में पाया जाता है। गॉल्जीकाय का एक अन्य महत्वपूर्ण कार्य कोशिका झिल्ली के निर्माण और मरम्मत में भाग लेना है। यह ग्लाइकोप्रोटीन और ग्लाइकोलिपिड के संश्लेषण में भी शामिल होता है, जो कोशिका की पहचान और संकेतन (signaling) के लिए आवश्यक हैं।

question:
Which bacteria have a thick cell wall with several layers of peptidoglycan and teichoic acid ?

[SSC CPO 2024]
options: Staphylococcus aureus
Pseudomonas aeruginosa
Salmonella enterica
Escherichia coli
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Staphylococcus aureus

Explanation:
Staphylococcus aureus is a Gram-positive bacterium that has a thick cell wall composed of multiple layers of peptidoglycan, providing structural stability. Additionally, it contains teichoic acid, which is embedded in the cell wall and plays a crucial role in bacterial identification and pathogenicity. The cell wall of Gram-positive bacteria is much thicker than that of Gram-negative bacteria due to the higher number of peptidoglycan layers. Other options like Pseudomonas, Salmonella, and E. coli are Gram-negative bacteria, which have a thin cell wall with only a single layer of peptidoglycan.

Extra Facts:
Gram-positive bacteria lack lipopolysaccharide (LPS), which is present in Gram-negative bacteria. The Gram staining technique is used to classify bacteria based on their cell wall composition. Gram-positive bacteria retain the crystal violet dye and appear blue/purple, while Gram-negative bacteria do not retain the dye and appear red/pink. Staphylococcus aureus can cause serious infections in humans, such as skin infections, pneumonia, and sepsis.

☛ What color do Gram-positive bacteria appear in Gram staining? → Blue/purple
☛ What is found in the cell wall of Gram-negative bacteria? → Thin peptidoglycan layer and lipopolysaccharide
☛ What type of bacterium is Staphylococcus aureus? → Gram-positive
☛ Give an example of a Gram-negative bacterium. → E. coli
question_hi:
किस जीवाणु में पेप्टीडोग्लाइकन और टाइकॉइक अम्ल की कई परतों के साथ मोटी कोशिका भित्ति होती है ?

[SSC CPO 2024]
options_hi: स्टेफिलोकॉकस ऑरियस (Staphylococcus aureus)
स्यूडोमोनास एरुगिनोसा (Pseudomonas aeruginosa)
साल्मोनेला एंटरिका (Salmonella enterica)
एशरिकिआ कोलाई (Escherichia coli)
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है स्टेफिलोकॉकस ऑरियस (Staphylococcus aureus)

Explanation:
स्टेफिलोकॉकस ऑरियस एक ग्राम-पॉजिटिव बैक्टीरिया है जिसमें मोटी कोशिका भित्ति होती है। इस भित्ति में पेप्टीडोग्लाइकन की कई परतें होती हैं, जो इसे संरचनात्मक स्थिरता प्रदान करती हैं। इसके अलावा, इसमें टाइकॉइक अम्ल भी पाया जाता है, जो कोशिका भित्ति से जुड़ा होता है और बैक्टीरिया की पहचान तथा रोगजनकता में महत्वपूर्ण भूमिका निभाता है। ग्राम-पॉजिटिव बैक्टीरिया की कोशिका भित्ति ग्राम-नेगेटिव बैक्टीरिया की तुलना में अधिक मोटी होती है, क्योंकि इसमें पेप्टीडोग्लाइकन की परतें अधिक होती हैं। अन्य विकल्प जैसे स्यूडोमोनास, साल्मोनेला, और ई. कोलाई ग्राम-नेगेटिव बैक्टीरिया हैं, जिनकी कोशिका भित्ति पतली होती है और इसमें पेप्टीडोग्लाइकन की केवल एक ही परत होती है।

Extra Facts:
ग्राम-पॉजिटिव बैक्टीरिया की कोशिका भित्ति में लिपोपॉलीसेकेराइड (LPS) नहीं होता, जबकि ग्राम-नेगेटिव बैक्टीरिया में यह पाया जाता है। ग्राम स्टेनिंग तकनीक का उपयोग बैक्टीरिया को उनकी कोशिका भित्ति के आधार पर वर्गीकृत करने के लिए किया जाता है। ग्राम-पॉजिटिव बैक्टीरिया क्रिस्टल वायलेट डाई को बनाए रखते हैं और नीले/बैंगनी दिखाई देते हैं, जबकि ग्राम-नेगेटिव बैक्टीरिया डाई को नहीं रोकते और लाल/गुलाबी दिखाई देते हैं। स्टेफिलोकॉकस ऑरियस मानव में त्वचा संक्रमण, निमोनिया, और सेप्सिस जैसी गंभीर बीमारियों का कारण बन सकता है।
